subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw change default web_fetch SSRF DNS handling so mixed allowed-plus-blocked result sets proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or should any blocked DNS answer continue to fail the request?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but it relaxes a default outbound security boundary and must reflect maintainer/security intent rather than automated policy guessing.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and cover mixed plus all-blocked cases in tests.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat the current behavior as intentional strict SSRF policy and document trusted proxy or explicit fake-IP configuration as the supported path for polluted DNS environments.

options.title: Make mixed-answer behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and cover mixed plus all-blocked cases in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The central SSRF assertion history and related maintainer discussion most directly point to steipete for the security-boundary decision.
